verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve behavior and keep the same messages and order. B moves more into the shared module: trimming, lowercasing and the optional-name rule are now options there. A leaves `trimmed(...).toLowerCase()` and the choice between required and length-only name checks in each handler, so some normalization is still duplicated and a fix may still have to be made twice. B's tests also cover more edge cases, such as non-string inputs and trimming to exactly 80 characters. Against that, B adds a code comment that points to a docs note that does not exist.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior identical, including the existing failure to lowercase invitation emails, and both flag that bug instead of fixing it. A consolidates more: each check does both normalization and validation, so handlers make one call per field and a fix to trimming or lowercasing happens in one place. B leaves `trimmed(...).toLowerCase()` repeated in the handlers and needs three lines per field. A's tests also cover more edge cases (non-string input, case preservation, the trimmed 80-character boundary), though its source comment points to a docs note that does not exist.
a_issues: The comment on `checkEmail` says to 'see the note in docs/api.md', but no such note exists. docs/api.md actually says invitation emails are stored lowercase, so the comment is misleading.
The `lowercase: false` option builds the known bug into the shared API as a supported configuration.
